requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.
rationale:
The one marked test, `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bootstrap_skill_is_bundled_and_directs_complete_inventories]`, adequately checks `requirements.cli.bootstrap_skill`. The requirement is about what a bundled skill document says, so checking that specific directive text is present is the right kind of test. I did not run the test; I checked its phrases against `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md`.

**Bundling.** The test asserts that `habeas-bootstrap-requirements` is in `SKILLS` and that its front-matter description starts with "Use when adopting Habeas in an existing codebase". The `SKILLS` check is tautological on its own, because `SKILLS` is a test constant. The skill is actually bundled by two other things:
- `skill_files`, which loads the skill text with `include_str!` from `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md`.
- The test `bundled_skills_are_five_skill_directories_each_home_to_its_topics`, which compares the skill directories on disk with `SKILLS`.

**Obligations and the assertions that cover them.** `assert_phrases` and `assert_in_order` run against the collapsed text of the skill, so line wrapping does not matter.

| Obligation | Assertions |
|---|---|
| Read the code and tests | "Read the existing requirements, documentation, public entry points, implementation, and tests" and "Follow behavior through the code". Both appear in step 2 of the skill. |
| Map every first-party test to a requirement or example | "every first-party runnable test or test case", "Record the behavior each test checks; fill in requirement names once they are installed", and "Every test must end up with a `{test}` reference to a requirement or example". |
| Identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality | "every function, method, struct, enum, and union, listed from the source rather than from the coverage warnings", "public APIs, commands, handlers, UI actions, configuration, outputs, errors, and distinct observable branches", "A tagged entry point doesn't mean every observable branch beneath it has a requirement", and "Give every inventoried test and each requirement's roots their references". |
| Report gaps and claim complete coverage only after an independent inventory review | Ordered assertions: step 8's "recount both inventories from the source and tests without your lists", then the gap-line format "- <item or behavior> (<file>:<line>): <reason>; <open question>", then "Claim 100% only when both inventories have no unmapped items", then "Don't silently exclude difficult cases". |

The ordering check matches the skill's structure: the recount step comes first, then the report format, then the condition for claiming 100%, then the "don't silently exclude" rule.

**Residual points.** None is a gap.
- The skill also says "Map each other inventoried item to the requirement whose root reaches it" and "An item that neither carries out a requirement nor serves other code goes on the gap list". The test does not assert these sentences. The assertion on "Give every inventoried test and each requirement's roots their references", together with the gap-list assertions, covers the mapping obligation closely enough.
- Another test, `bundled_skills_mark_roots_and_handle_uncovered_items`, also exercises related text.

No acknowledgments apply.
